description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. A four-lobed Billow sign sits at the center in place of a sigil, at moderate size, a little over a third of the ring's radius. Three Rain signs sit in the outer part of the ring: one at east-northeast, one at east-southeast, and one at west-southwest. Each is a square with concave sides and short ticked lines on its edges. They are drawn the same way, and none is clearly flipped inside-out. A small Concealment sign, an eight-armed star with tiny eye marks, sits between the Billow sign and the east-southeast Rain sign. There is no element sigil and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Billow takes the center and sets the core behavior: turning available material into a soft, fluffy cloud. Its moderate size points to a moderate intensity. Rain summons the target material, making it fall from above. None of the Rain signs is turned inside-out, so all three act normally rather than pushing material away. Rain is semi-directional, so its rotation does not steer the spell. Two of the three Rain signs sit on the east side, so the effect is unevenly spread. Reading this as a lean toward the east is a guess. The single Concealment sign adds a hiding effect to what the seal produces. Without an element sigil, the spell is not tied to one element and works on whatever material it summons.
effect: Summons material to fall over the area like rainfall and turns it into soft, fluffy cloud, with the cloud or what it covers kept hidden from view. The effect is likely heavier on the eastern side.
